q: Blessed indeed is the Being Who revealed the Decider
(the Qur'aan, which differentiates between right and wrong, Halaal and Haraam, etc)
so that he may be a Warner to the universe.
v.s: Blessed is He who sent down the Criterion upon His Servant that he may be to the worlds a warner -
v.c: Blessed is the One Who sent down the Standard to His servant, so that he may be a warner to the whole world.

q: The One to Whom belongs the kingdom of the heavens and the earth, Who has not taken any son
has no partner in the kingdom
has created everything, and then meticulously perfected them
(He ordained everything in its exact manner).
v.s: He to whom belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth and who has not taken a son and has not had a partner in dominion and has created each thing and determined it with [precise] determination.
v.c: ˹Allah is˺ the One to Whom belongs the kingdom of the heavens and the earth, Who has never had ˹any˺ offspring, nor does He have a partner in ˹governing˺ the kingdom. He has created everything, ordaining it precisely.

q: adopt Aaliha who cannot create anything, but have themselves been created. They have no power to effect any harm nor any benefit to themselves, and do not have any power over life, death or resurrection.
(When they are so helpless, how can they be worshipped?)
v.s: But they have taken besides Him gods which create nothing, while they are created, and possess not for themselves any harm or benefit and possess not [power to cause] death or life or resurrection.
v.c: Yet they have taken besides Him gods who cannot create anything but are themselves created. Nor can they protect or benefit themselves. Nor can they control life, death, or resurrection.

q: is merely a lie that he
has forged and which other people
They have indeed presented a grave injustice and lie.
(see Surah 16, verse 103 where Allaah makes it clear that it is impossible for a non-Arab to produce a book that even the most eloquent Arabs could not produce.)
v.s: And those who disbelieve say, "This [Qur’ān] is not except a falsehood he invented, and another people assisted him in it." But they have committed an injustice and a lie.
v.c: The disbelievers say, “This ˹Quran˺ is nothing but a fabrication which he made up with the help of others.” Their claim is totally unjustified and untrue!

q: “Fables of the old men that he
(These were the two appointed times of prayers at first.)
v.s: And they say, "Legends of the former peoples which he has written down, and they are dictated to him morning and afternoon."
v.c: And they say, “˹These revelations are only˺ ancient fables which he has had written down, and they are rehearsed to him morning and evening.”

q: Say, “The One Who knows the secrets of the heavens and the earth has revealed it
(for someone without this knowledge can never produce such a masterpiece).
Certainly, He has always been the Most Forgiving, the Most Merciful
(and will therefore not punish them immediately for their insolence but gives them time to repent).'
v.s: Say, [O Muhammad], “It has been revealed by He who knows [every] secret within the heavens and the earth. Indeed, He is ever Forgiving and Merciful.”
v.c: Say, ˹O Prophet,˺ “This ˹Quran˺ has been revealed by the One Who knows the secrets of the heavens and the earth. Surely He is All-Forgiving, Most Merciful.”

q: say, “What is the matter with this Rasool that he eats food and walks in the marketplaces
Why is an angel not sent with him to be a warner alongside him?”
v.s: And they say, "What is this messenger that eats food and walks in the markets? Why was there not sent down to him an angel so he would be with him a warner?
v.c: And they say ˹mockingly˺, “What kind of messenger is this who eats food and goes about in market-places ˹for a living˺? If only an angel had been sent down with him to be his co-warner,

q: “...Or why is a treasure not given to him or why does he not have an orchard from which he may eat?”

(Allaah did not allow Rasulullaah ﷺ to demonstrate to the people these miracles because they would have rejected them and thereby attracted Allaah's immediate punishment.) (Not satisfied with saying only this,)
(to the Muslims to prevent them from following Rasulullaah ﷺ),
“You are merely following a bewitched man!”
v.s: Or [why is not] a treasure presented to him [from heaven], or does he [not] have a garden from which he eats?" And the wrongdoers say, "You follow not but a man affected by magic."
v.c: or a treasure had been cast down to him, or he had had a garden from which he may eat!” And the wrongdoers say ˹to the believers˺, “You are only following a bewitched man.”

q: (when they are unable to present any credible argument)!
astray and will not find any road
v.s: Look how they strike for you comparisons; but they have strayed, so they cannot [find] a way.
v.c: See ˹O Prophet˺ how they call you names! So they have gone so ˹far˺ astray that they cannot find the ˹Right˺ Way.

q: Blessed is that Being Who, if He willed, would have granted you better bounties than this
by way of gardens beneath which rivers flow and He would have made palaces for you.
(However, Allaah had not done this because it was unnecessary and would have been harmful for them.)
v.s: Blessed is He who, if He willed, could have made for you [something] better than that - gardens beneath which rivers flow - and could make for you palaces.
v.c: Blessed is the One Who—if He wills—can give you far better than ˹all˺ that: gardens under which rivers flow, and palaces as well.

q: (their main reason for rejecting the message of Rasulullaah ﷺ is that)
they reject Qiyaamah and We have prepared the Blaze
v.s: But they have denied the Hour, and We have prepared for those who deny the Hour a Blaze.
v.c: In fact, they deny the Hour. And for the deniers of the Hour, We have prepared a blazing Fire.

q: will see them from a distance
(on the Day of Qiyaamah), (it will be so intense that)
they will hear the roar of its fury and its crackling
v.s: When it [i.e., the Hellfire] sees them from a distant place, they will hear its fury and roaring.
v.c: Once it sees them from a distance, they will hear it fuming and growling.

q: When they are flung into a narrow place
with their hands and feet in shackles, they will cry out for destruction
(they will plead for death to come to them).
v.s: And when they are thrown into a narrow place therein bound in chains, they will cry out thereupon for destruction.
v.c: And when they are tossed into a narrow place inside ˹Hell˺, chained together, then and there they will cry out for ˹instant˺ destruction.

q: “Do not cry for only one destruction
today, but cry for many a destruction
(regardless of how much you wish for it, death will never come to you and you will suffer here forever).”
v.s: [They will be told], "Do not cry this Day for one destruction but cry for much destruction."
v.c: ˹They will be told,˺ “Do not cry only once for destruction, but cry many times over!”

q: better, or the Jannah of eternity that those with Taqwa have been promised. It shall be a reward and an abode
v.s: Say, "Is that better or the Garden of Eternity which is promised to the righteous? It will be for them a reward and destination.
v.c: Say, ˹O Prophet,˺ “Is this better or the Garden of Eternity which the righteous have been promised, as a reward and ˹an ultimate˺ destination?

q: There they shall have whatever they desire and they will live there forever
This is a promise that your Rabb has undertaken to fulfil
and for which He should be asked.
(man should constantly pray to Allaah to enter him into Jannah.)
v.s: For them therein is whatever they wish, [while] abiding eternally. It is ever upon your Lord a promise [worthy to be] requested.
v.c: There they will have whatever they wish for, forever. That is a promise ˹to be sought after˺, binding on your Lord.”

q: together with those whom they worship besides Allaah, will be gathered together and Allaah will ask
“Did you lead these bondsmen of Mine astray, or did they themselves
v.s: And [mention] the Day He will gather them and that which they worship besides God and will say, "Did you mislead these, My servants, or did they [themselves] stray from the way?"
v.c: ˹Watch for˺ the Day He will gather them along with what they used to worship besides Allah, and ask ˹the objects of worship˺, “Was it you who misled these servants of Mine, or did they stray from the Way ˹on their own˺?”

q: It was not befitting for us to take
any friends besides You, but what happened was that You granted enjoyment
(became so engrossed in these things that they)
v.s: They will say, "Exalted are You! It was not for us to take besides You any allies [i.e., protectors]. But You provided comforts for them and their fathers until they forgot the message and became a people ruined."
v.c: They will say, “Glory be to You! It was not right for ˹others like˺ us to take any lords besides You, but You allowed enjoyment for them and their forefathers ˹for so long˺ that they forgot ˹Your˺ remembrance and became a doomed people.”

q: (It will then be said to the Mushrikeen)
(that you worshipped them for their pleasure).
neither be able to turn the punishment away nor receive any assistance
(from anyone to rescue you from the punishment).
We shall inflict a grievous punishment on those of you who are oppressive
v.s: So they will deny you, [disbelievers], in what you say, and you cannot avert [punishment] or [find] help. And whoever commits injustice among you - We will make him taste a great punishment.
v.c: ˹The doomed will be told˺, “Your gods have clearly denied your claims. So now you can neither ward off ˹the punishment˺ nor get any help.” And whoever of you does wrong, We will make them taste a horrible punishment.

q: All the Ambiyaa that We sent before you
used to eat food and walk in the marketplaces
(because they too were humans, which is perfectly in order). (Therefore, do not worry about the persistent taunts of the Kuffaar because)
We have made some of you as trials
(to see whether you will exercise patience).
(so beware of what you do and know that He will reward every good deed that you do).
v.s: And We did not send before you, [O Muhammad], any of the messengers except that they ate food and walked in the markets. And We have made some of you [people] as trial for others - will you have patience? And ever is your Lord, Seeing.
v.c: We never sent any messenger before you ˹O Prophet˺, who did not eat food and go about in market-places. We have made some of you a trial for others. Will you ˹not then˺ be patient? And your Lord is All-Seeing.

q: to meet Us say, “Why are angels not sent to us
or why do we not see our Rabb
They are certainly proud of themselves
(because of which they make such absurd demands).
v.s: And those who do not expect the meeting with Us say, "Why were not angels sent down to us, or [why] do we [not] see our Lord?" They have certainly become arrogant within themselves and [become] insolent with great insolence.
v.c: Those who do not expect to meet Us say, “If only the angels were sent down to us, or we could see our Lord!” They have certainly been carried away by their arrogance and have entirely exceeded all limits.

q: There shall be no good news
and they will shout, “Stay far away!”
(This was exactly what they used to tell the Ambiyaa ﵊ in the world. However, on the Day of Qiyaamah, they will say these words to protect themselves from punishment.)
v.s: The day they see the angels - no good tidings will there be that day for the criminals, and [the angels] will say, "Prevented and inaccessible."
v.c: ˹But˺ on the Day they will see the angels, there will be no good news for the wicked, who will cry, “Keep away! Away ˹from us˺!”

q: deeds and reduce them to scattered dust
(render them worthless because they were carried out without Imaan).
v.s: And We will approach [i.e., regard] what they have done of deeds and make them as dust dispersed.
v.c: Then We will turn to whatever ˹good˺ deeds they did, reducing them to scattered dust.

q: The people of Jannah will be in the best of abodes and the best of resting places
v.s: The companions of Paradise, that Day, are [in] a better settlement and better resting place.
v.c: ˹But˺ on that Day the residents of Paradise will have the best settlement and the finest place to rest.

q: when the sky will be split and from the clouds the angels will descend in large numbers
v.s: And [mention] the Day when the heaven will split open with [emerging] clouds, and the angels will be sent down in successive descent.
v.c: ˹Watch for˺ the Day the heavens will burst with clouds, and the angels will be sent down in successive ranks.

q: True sovereignty on that day will be exclusive
(because no one else will even be able to claim ownership over anything).
The day will be very difficult for the Kaafiroon
(because they will be condemned to eternal punishment).
v.s: True sovereignty, that Day, is for the Most Merciful. And it will be upon the disbelievers a difficult Day.
v.c: True authority on that Day will belong ˹only˺ to the Most Compassionate. And it will be a hard day for the disbelievers.

q: (the Mushrik Uqba bin Abi Mu'eet, who forsook Islaam to please his friend Ubay bin Khalaf)
saying,' 'If only I had chosen the path
v.s: And the Day the wrongdoer will bite on his hands [in regret] he will say, "Oh, I wish I had taken with the Messenger a way.
v.c: And ˹beware of˺ the Day the wrongdoer will bite his nails ˹in regret˺ and say, “Oh! I wish I had followed the Way along with the Messenger!

q: “...Woe to me! If only I had never taken such a person
(for I would have then remained a Muslim and would not be condemned to Jahannam today).'
v.s: Oh, woe to me! I wish I had not taken that one as a friend.
v.c: Woe to me! I wish I had never taken so-and-so as a close friend.

q: has certainly deviated me from the reminder
after it had come to me.” Shaytaan always deserts
(when man is in need after following Shaytaan's deceptions).
v.s: He led me away from the remembrance after it had come to me. And ever is Satan, to man, a deserter."
v.c: It was he who truly made me stray from the Reminder after it had reached me.” And Satan has always betrayed humanity.

q: (attesting to the kufr of his people),
“O my Rabb! My people have ignored this Qur'aan
v.s: And the Messenger has said, "O my Lord, indeed my people have taken this Qur’ān as [a thing] abandoned."
v.c: The Messenger has cried, “O my Lord! My people have indeed received this Quran with neglect.”

q: We have appointed from the criminals
(However, the Ambiyaa ﵊ had no cause to fear their enemies because)
Your Rabb suffices as a Guide and a Helper
(He will make you reach the desired destination).
v.s: And thus have We made for every prophet an enemy from among the criminals. But sufficient is your Lord as a guide and a helper.
v.c: Similarly, We made enemies for every prophet from among the wicked, but sufficient is your Lord as a Guide and Helper.

q: Those who commit kufr say, “Why is the entire Qur'aan not revealed to him
We have revealed it in this manner
(part by part over a period of approximately 23 years)
(when it provides you with encouragement each time you require it),
(slowly so that it is easier to understand and easier to memorise).
v.s: And those who disbelieve say, "Why was the Qur’ān not revealed to him all at once?" Thus [it is] that We may strengthen thereby your heart. And We have spaced it distinctly.
v.c: The disbelievers say, “If only the Quran had been sent down to him all at once!” ˹We have sent it˺ as such ˹in stages˺ so We may reassure your heart with it. And We have revealed it at a deliberate pace.

q: (to falsify and find fault with your message),
We reveal the precise reply to you with explicit clarity
(so that you may counter their words with something better).
v.s: And they do not come to you with an example [i.e., argument] except that We bring you the truth and the best explanation.
v.c: Whenever they bring you an argument, We come to you with the right refutation and the best explanation.

q: on their faces will certainly be in the worst of predicaments
and most deviated from the path
v.s: The ones who are gathered on their faces to Hell - those are the worst in position and farthest astray in [their] way.
v.c: Those who will be dragged into Hell on their faces will be in the worst place, and are ˹now˺ farthest from the ˹Right˺ Way.

q: to Moosa ﵊ and made his brother Haaroon ﵊ a minister
v.s: And We had certainly given Moses the Scripture and appointed with him his brother Aaron as an assistant.
v.c: We certainly gave Moses the Book and appointed his brother Aaron as his helper.

q: We then said, “The two of you should go
to the nation that rejects Our Aayaat
(Fir'oun's nation).” (When the two brothers preached Towheed to Fir'oun and his people, they rejected the message.)
(of Fir'oun when We drowned them in the Red Sea).
v.s: And We said, "Go both of you to the people who have denied Our signs." Then We destroyed them with [complete] destruction.
v.c: We had ordered ˹them˺, “Go to the people who would deny Our signs.” Then We annihilated the deniers entirely.

q: And We drowned the people of Nooh ﵊ when they rejected the Rusul
(by rejecting the message of Nooh ﵊ they actually rejected all the Rusul because each one carried the same message),
making them a lesson to people.
(In addition to this punishment in the world,)
v.s: And the people of Noah - when they denied the messengers, We drowned them, and We made them for mankind a sign. And We have prepared for the wrongdoers a painful punishment.
v.c: And when the people of Noah rejected the messengers, We drowned them, making them an example to humanity. And We have prepared a painful punishment for the wrongdoers.

q: (Just as the destruction of this nation is a lesson, do not forget that)
We also annihilated the Aad, the Thamud, the people of the well
(a community of Kuffaar that was swallowed by the earth as they sat beside a well)
v.s: And [We destroyed] ʿAad and Thamūd and the companions of the well and many generations between them.
v.c: Also ˹We destroyed˺ ’Ȃd, Thamûd, and the people of the Water-pit, as well as many peoples in between.

q: (when they refused to accept imaan, We)
v.s: And for each We presented examples [as warnings], and each We destroyed with [total] destruction.
v.c: For each We set forth ˹various˺ lessons, and We ultimately destroyed each.

q: that was showered by a devastating rain
(because their behaviour indicates that they have not)?
(it is not that they have not seen it), (they have definitely seen the ruins of this place)
(they refuse to take a lesson because)
they are not expecting any resurrection.
(Because they do not believe in resurrection, they do not fear the punishment of the Aakhirah and therefore fail to learn a lesson from the destruction of previous nations.)
v.s: And they have already come upon the town which was showered with a rain of evil [i.e., stones]. So have they not seen it? But they are not expecting resurrection.
v.c: They have certainly passed by the city ˹of Sodom˺, which had been showered with a dreadful rain ˹of stones˺. Have they not seen its ruins? But they do not expect to be resurrected.

q: they seek only to mock you
“Has Allaah sent him as a Rasool
(Could Allaah not find someone else with more wealth and higher social standing)?”
v.s: And when they see you, [O Muhammad], they take you not except in ridicule, [saying], “Is this the one whom God has sent as a messenger?
v.c: When they see you ˹O Prophet˺, they only make fun of you, ˹saying,˺ “Is this the one that Allah has sent as a messenger?

q: would have led us away from our gods if we had not
persevered with them.” Shortly, when they see the punishment
they will come to know who has strayed most from the path.
(They will then realise that it was they rather than Rasulullaah ﷺ and the Mu'mineen who had strayed from the path of salvation.)
v.s: He almost would have misled us from our gods had we not been steadfast in [worship of] them." But they are going to know, when they see the punishment, who is farthest astray in [his] way.
v.c: He would have almost tricked us away from our gods, had we not been so devoted to them.” ˹But˺ soon they will know, when they face the punishment, who is far astray from the ˹Right˺ Way.

q: Have you seen the one who has taken his whims
(one who does whatever his desires dictate)?
Will you be a guardian over him

(constantly checking his actions.)? (You have no control over his beliefs and actions and should therefore not be grieved when he refuses to accept imaan. His fault is not your responsibility at all.)
v.s: Have you seen the one who takes as his god his own desire? Then would you be responsible for him?
v.c: Have you seen ˹O Prophet˺ the one who has taken their own desires as their god? Will you then be a keeper over them?

q: Or do you think that most of them hear
(everything they are told)? (This is not the case because)
They are merely like animals, but even more astray.
(Whereas animals still realise that they should avoid things that cause them harm, the Kuffaar plunge further into kufr and sin that will cause them the worst harm in both worlds.)
v.s: Or do you think that most of them hear or reason? They are not except like livestock. Rather, they are [even] more astray in [their] way.
v.c: Or do you think that most of them listen or understand? They are only like cattle—no, more than that, they are astray from the ˹Right˺ Way!

q: Do you not see how your Rabb spreads
(causes it to extend as the afternoon progresses).
If He willed, He could have made it stationary.
(It is therefore only because of Allaah's will that shadows move.) (However,)
We then appoint the sun as a guide to it

(the shadow). (Although the shadow falls and moves solely because of Allaah's power, Allaah has made the sun and the movement of the earth signs for man to understand the falling of the shadow. It is not the sun nor the earth's movement that are responsible for the shadow falling, but they are merely instruments. Man should therefore not think that things happen because of the visible means that he sees. Everything happens by Allaah's will.)
v.s: Have you not considered your Lord - how He extends the shadow, and if He willed, He could have made it stationary? Then We made the sun for it an indication.
v.c: Have you not seen how your Lord extends the shade—He could have simply made it ˹remain˺ still if He so willed—then We make the sun its guide,
v.h: Allah’s Power: 1) The Sun and Shade

q: (causing it to shorten as the morning passes).
v.s: Then We hold it in hand for a brief grasp.
v.c: causing the shade to retreat gradually?

q: Allaah is the One Who has made the night as a garment
(which covers the earth and conceals things as clothes do),
has made sleep a form of rest and has made the day a time
(on earth in search of their provisions because it is a time when they can see clearly and do much more).
v.s: And it is He who has made the night for you as clothing and sleep [a means for] rest and has made the day a resurrection.
v.c: He is the One Who has made the night for you as a cover, and ˹made˺ sleep for resting, and the day for rising.

q: He is the One Who sends the winds as a carrier of good news ahead of His mercy
(the winds precede the rain that is due to arrive).
And He sends from the skies water that purifies.
v.s: And it is He who sends the winds as good tidings before His mercy [i.e., rainfall], and We send down from the sky pure water
v.c: And He is the One Who sends the winds ushering in His mercy, and We send down pure rain from the sky,

q: So that We revive the dead
and so that We give drinking water to Our creation,
v.s: That We may bring to life thereby a dead land and give it as drink to those We created of numerous livestock and men.
v.c: giving life to a lifeless land, and providing water for countless animals and humans of Our Own creation.

q: but most people only wish to be ungrateful.
v.s: And We have certainly distributed it among them that they might be reminded, but most of the people refuse except disbelief.
v.c: We certainly disperse it among them so they may be mindful, but most people persist in ungratefulness.

q: If We willed, We would have sent a
(However, We sent many Ambiyaa as warners to several towns.)
v.s: And if We had willed, We could have sent into every city a warner.
v.c: Had We willed, We could have easily sent a warner to every society.

q: (the Qur'aan). (Use the teachings of the Qur'aan to oppose the false beliefs and actions of the Kuffaar.)
v.s: So do not obey the disbelievers, and strive against them with it [i.e., the Qur’ān] a great striving.
v.c: So do not yield to the disbelievers, but strive diligently against them with this ˹Quran˺.

q: being sweet and quenching, while the other
is salty and bitter. He has created between them a barrier that acts as an impregnable
(which prevents the two types of water from mixing even though they run into each other).
v.s: And it is He who has released [simultaneously] the two seas [i.e., bodies of water], one fresh and sweet and one salty and bitter, and He placed between them a barrier and prohibiting partition.
v.c: And He is the One Who merges the two bodies of water: one fresh and palatable and the other salty and bitter, placing between them a barrier they cannot cross.

q: It is He Who has created man from water
(to extend and enrich man's social life, Allaah)
has appointed for him relatives by blood and relatives by marriage. Your Rabb is Ever Powerful
v.s: And it is He who has created from water [i.e., semen] a human being and made him [a relative by] lineage and marriage. And ever is your Lord competent [concerning creation].
v.c: And He is the One Who creates human beings from a ˹humble˺ liquid, then establishes for them bonds of kinship and marriage. For your Lord is Most Capable.

q: (However, despite all these favours that Allaah has given man,)
worship things that do not benefit them, nor harm them
The Kaafir was ever opposed to
(by following the dictates of Shaytaan his enemy rather than the commands of Allaah, Who gave him everything he has).
v.s: But they worship rather than God that which does not benefit them or harm them, and the disbeliever is ever, against his Lord, an assistant [to Satan].
v.c: Yet they worship besides Allah what can neither benefit nor harm them. And the disbeliever always collaborates against their Lord.

q: only as a carrier of good news
v.s: And We have not sent you, [O Muhammad], except as a bringer of good tidings and a warner.
v.c: And We have sent you ˹O Prophet˺ only as a deliverer of good news and a warner.
v.h: Advice to the Prophet: Trust in Allah

q: “I do not ask you for any payment
(for the message I am conveying to you)
apart from being the person who wishes to tread a path towards his Rabb
(having such faithful followers is all I ask for, not any other payment).”
v.s: Say, "I do not ask of you for it any payment - only that whoever wills might take to his Lord a way."
v.c: Say, “I do not ask you for any reward for this ˹message˺, but whoever wishes, let them pursue the Way to their Lord.”

q: Who cannot die and glorify His praises. Allaah suffices as the Knower of His bondsmen's sins
(even if there was nothing else to witness man's sins, Allaah's knowledge is sufficient to prove him guilty).
v.s: And rely upon the Ever-Living who does not die, and exalt [God] with His praise. And sufficient is He to be, with the sins of His servants, Acquainted -
v.c: Put your trust in the Ever-Living, Who never dies, and glorify His praises. Sufficient is He as All-Aware of the sins of His servants.

q: It was He Who created the heavens, the earth and whatever is between them in six days, and then turned
to the Throne. He is the Most Merciful, so enquire about Him from one who is knowledgeable.
(Find out about Allaah from those who have recognised Him so that you may also recognise Him.)
v.s: He who created the heavens and the earth and what is between them in six days and then established Himself above the Throne - the Most Merciful, so ask about Him one well informed [i.e., the Prophet (ﷺ)].
v.c: ˹He is˺ the One Who created the heavens and the earth and everything in between in six Days, then established Himself on the Throne. ˹He is˺ the Most Compassionate! Ask ˹none other than˺ the All-Knowledgeable about Himself.

q: are told, “Prostrate to Ar Rahmaan,” they
“What is Ar Rahmaan? Should we prostrate to whatever you command us?” Their hatred then only increases.
(One who recites or hears this verse being recited should perform Sajdah.)
v.s: And when it is said to them, "Prostrate to the Most Merciful," they say, "And what is the Most Merciful? Should we prostrate to that which you order us?" And it increases them in aversion.
v.c: When it is said to them, “Prostrate to the Most Compassionate,” they ask ˹in disgust˺, “What is ‘the Most Compassionate’? Will we prostrate to whatever you order us to?” And it only drives them farther away.

q: Blessed is the Being Who created gigantic stars in the sky and
(among the more prominent sources of light that He created in the sky, He has)
placed the sun and the luminous moon in it.
v.s: Blessed is He who has placed in the sky great stars and placed therein a [burning] lamp and luminous moon.
v.c: Blessed is the One Who has placed constellations in the sky, as well as a ˹radiant˺ lamp and a luminous moon.

q: It is He Who has appointed the night and the day in succession for the one who intends to take heed (reflect) or who intends to be grateful.
(It is such people who appreciate these favours of Allaah and use them in obedience to Him.)
v.s: And it is He who has made the night and the day in succession for whoever desires to remember or desires gratitude.
v.c: And He is the One Who causes the day and the night to alternate, ˹as a sign˺ for whoever desires to be mindful or to be grateful.

q: Ar Rahmaan's bondsmen are those who walk on earth in humility
and, when the ignorant talk to them, they
(Leave us in peace). (By doing this, they avoid useless talk and senseless arguments.)
v.s: And the servants of the Most Merciful are those who walk upon the earth easily, and when the ignorant address them [harshly], they say [words of] peace,
v.c: The ˹true˺ servants of the Most Compassionate are those who walk on the earth humbly, and when the foolish address them ˹improperly˺, they only respond with peace.

q: Those who spend the night in prostrating and standing before their Rabb
v.s: And those who spend [part of] the night to their Lord prostrating and standing [in prayer]
v.c: ˹They are˺ those who spend ˹a good portion of˺ the night, prostrating themselves and standing before their Lord. 3) ˹Hope and˺ Fear

q: Those who say, “O our Rabb! Turn the punishment of Jahannam away from us. Verily its punishment is devastating indeed!”
v.s: And those who say, "Our Lord, avert from us the punishment of Hell. Indeed, its punishment is ever adhering;
v.c: ˹They are˺ those who pray, “Our Lord! Keep the punishment of Hell away from us, for its punishment is indeed unrelenting.

q: is surely an evil residence and abode.”
v.s: Indeed, it is evil as a settlement and residence."
v.c: It is certainly an evil place to settle and reside.”

q: Those who, when they spend, are neither extravagant
nor miserly, but are rather stationed
(extremes. They neither spend too much nor too little).
v.s: And [they are] those who, when they spend, do so not excessively or sparingly but are ever, between that, [justly] moderate
v.c: ˹They are˺ those who spend neither wastefully nor stingily, but moderately in between.

q: Those who do not call to
another Ilaah with Allaah, who only kill a soul forbidden by Allaah with a warrant
(when required to execute a person whom a court of Shari'ah sentences to death),
(they neither engage in fornication nor adultery).
(sins of Shirk, murder, fornication or adultery)
shall meet with a grave punishment.
v.s: And those who do not invoke with God another deity or kill the soul which God has forbidden [to be killed], except by right, and do not commit unlawful sexual intercourse. And whoever should do that will meet a penalty.
v.c: ˹They are˺ those who do not invoke any other god besides Allah, nor take a ˹human˺ life—made sacred by Allah—except with ˹legal˺ right, nor commit fornication. And whoever does ˹any of˺ this will face the penalty.

q: Punishment will be multiplied for him on the Day of Qiyaamah and he shall remain disgraced in it
v.s: Multiplied for him is the punishment on the Day of Resurrection, and he will abide therein humiliated -
v.c: Their punishment will be multiplied on the Day of Judgment, and they will remain in it forever, in disgrace.

q: (This punishment is for all such people)
repent, accept Imaan and perform good actions. For such people Allaah will convert their sins into good deeds. Allaah is Ever Most Forgiving, Most Merciful
v.s: Except for those who repent, believe and do righteous work. For them God will replace their evil deeds with good. And ever is God Forgiving and Merciful.
v.c: As for those who repent, believe, and do good deeds, they are the ones whose evil deeds Allah will change into good deeds. For Allah is All-Forgiving, Most Merciful.

q: Whoever repents and performs good actions has certainly turned to Allaah in earnestness
v.s: And he who repents and does righteousness does indeed turn to God with [accepted] repentance.
v.c: And whoever repents and does good has truly turned to Allah properly.

q: those who do not engage in acts of deceit
(do not take false oaths and give false evidence)
and, when they pass by frivolous
(without participating and without unnecessarily arguing with the participants).
v.s: And [they are] those who do not testify to falsehood, and when they pass near ill speech, they pass by with dignity.
v.c: ˹They are˺ those who do not bear false witness, and when they come across falsehood, they pass ˹it˺ by with dignity.

q: Those who, when they are reminded by the Aayaat
of their Rabb, do not fall down
(Rather, they heed the advice given and see the truth).
v.s: And those who, when reminded of the verses of their Lord, do not fall upon them deaf and blind.
v.c: ˹They are˺ those who, when reminded of the revelation of their Lord, do not turn a blind eye or a deaf ear to it.

q: Those who say, “O our Rabb! Grant us the coolness
(so that they never become a source of regret or distress for us in either world when they follow Islaam properly),
(make our progeny pious and make us pious enough to guide pious people).'
v.s: And those who say, "Our Lord, grant us from among our wives and offspring comfort to our eyes and make us a leader [i.e., example] for the righteous."
v.c: ˹They are˺ those who pray, “Our Lord! Bless us with ˹pious˺ spouses and offspring who will be the joy of our hearts, and make us models for the righteous.”

q: These people, because of their steadfastness
(which will increase their honour and reverence).
v.s: Those will be awarded the Chamber for what they patiently endured, and they will be received therein with greetings and [words of] peace,
v.c: It is they who will be rewarded with ˹elevated˺ mansions ˹in Paradise˺ for their perseverance, and will be received with salutations and ˹greetings of˺ peace,

q: forever. It is surely a beautiful residence and abode.
v.s: Abiding eternally therein. Good is the settlement and residence.
v.c: staying there forever. What an excellent place to settle and reside!

q: Say, “My Rabb would not concern Himself with you if it had not been for your du'aa
v.s: Say, "What would my Lord care for you if not for your supplication?" For you [disbelievers] have denied, so it [i.e., your denial] is going to be adherent.
v.c: Say, ˹O Prophet,˺ “You ˹all˺ would not ˹even˺ matter to my Lord were it not for your faith ˹in Him˺. But now you ˹disbelievers˺ have denied ˹the truth˺, so the torment is bound to come.”
